# ledger_api_token (Resource)

An API token of Ledger. Ledger generates the token and shows it **once**, when it is created; this resource keeps it in the `secret` attribute.

~> **The token is stored in the Terraform state.** This is the one secret the provider keeps in state (every other secret is write-only), because Ledger, not you, generates it. Encrypt the state, restrict who can read it, prefer short-lived tokens (`expires_at`) and narrow `grants`, and treat the state like the token. `secret` is marked sensitive, which hides it from plan output only. Never print it with `output` unless that output is also `sensitive = true`.

A token cannot be changed: changing any argument **replaces** it (the old one is revoked, then a new one is created). Destroying the resource **revokes** the token at once, and Ledger also revokes every token created through it.

Tokens created this way are owned by the root account and bounded by its role. Reading token metadata needs an API token with the `tokens:read` grant; revoking needs `tokens:write`. **Creating a token needs the root token of the root account** (the first user, normally created with `ledger token create --create administrator --root` on the Ledger host): Ledger refuses `POST /auth/tokens` for any other API token with 403 `forbidden`. Revoking a root token needs the root token too (`root_token_required`).

Not importable: Ledger never serves a token again, so an imported token would have no secret. Use the `ledger_api_token` data source to read the metadata of tokens that exist.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# WARNING: the token Ledger generates is stored in the Terraform state (sensitive, but not encrypted by Terraform).
# Protect and encrypt the state, prefer a short expiry and narrow grants.
#
# Creating a token needs the provider to run with the ROOT token of the root account (the one created on the Ledger
# host with: ledger token create --create administrator --root). Any other token is refused.
resource "ledger_api_token" "reporting" {
  name   = "monthly-reporting"
  grants = ["commitments:read", "organisation:read"]

  # Optional. Without it the token never expires. Ledger may cap it at the expiry of the creating token.
  expires_at = "2030-01-31T00:00:00Z"
}

# A token cannot be changed: changing any argument replaces it (the old one is revoked).
# Hand the secret on only to a sensitive place; never print it in a plain output.
output "reporting_token" {
  value     = ledger_api_token.reporting.secret
  sensitive = true
}

# A root token holds every grant of its owner's role. Prefer narrow grants.
resource "ledger_api_token" "automation_root" {
  name = "automation-root"
  root = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) A name to recognise the token by, 1 to 100 characters. Changing it replaces the token.

### Optional

- `expires_at` (String) When the token expires (RFC 3339, in the future). Without it the token never expires. Ledger caps it at the expiry of the creating token, silently: see `effective_expires_at` for what applies. Changing it replaces the token.
- `grants` (Set of String) The grants the token holds (see the `ledger_grants` data source), at least one unless `root` is true. Each must be held by the creating root token; an unknown grant is refused. Requests get only the grants the owner's current role allows. Changing it replaces the token.
- `root` (Boolean) Create a **root token**: it holds every grant its owner's role holds, now and in later versions, and can itself create tokens. Defaults to `false`. Set either `grants` or `root = true`, not both. Prefer narrow grants. Changing it replaces the token.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the token was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `effective_expires_at` (String) The expiry Ledger applies (RFC 3339, UTC), or null when the token never expires. It differs from `expires_at` when Ledger capped it.
- `hint` (String) The prefix and the first and last characters of the token, to recognise it (not secret).
- `id` (String) The Ledger identifier of the token (a ULID).
- `last_chars` (String) The last four characters.
- `last_used_at` (String) When it was last used (updated at most once a minute), or null.
- `owner_id` (String) The user that owns the token (the root account).
- `parent_token_id` (String) The token that created this one through the API, or null.
- `prefix` (String) `ldgr_` and the first four random characters.
- `revoked_at` (String) When it was revoked, or null.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The token itself (`ldgr_…`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. **Stored in the Terraform state**: protect the state. Ledger shows it only at creation and cannot return it later.
- `status` (String) `active`, `expired` or `revoked`, as last read. A token revoked outside Terraform is removed from state on refresh, so the next apply creates a new one.
- `warning` (String) What a root token can do, as stated by Ledger when it was created; null for other tokens.
